Motivation: To improve the quality of images produced by Stable Diffusion by addressing the limitations of current generative methods, particularly in reducing artifacts and enhancing semantic fidelity.

Method: The proposed system utilizes a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence LLM for generating optimized negative prompts and a CNN-RNN hybrid classifier for evaluating diffusion steps and guiding latent-space updates.

Result: Experimental results indicate that the dual-guidance framework effectively reduces artifacts and enhances the semantic quality of generated images compared to existing baseline techniques.

Conclusion: The integration of negative prompt optimization with classifier guidance significantly elevates the performance of image generation in Stable Diffusion.

Abstract: We present a novel system that integrates negative prompt optimization via a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence LLM and latent-space classifier guidance to improve the quality of images generated by Stable Diffusion. Our approach automatically generates optimized negative prompts, and employs a CNN-RNN hybrid classifier to evaluate and guide diffusion steps, rolling back low-quality latent updates. Experimental results demonstrate that our dual-guidance framework reduces artifacts and improves semantic fidelity compared to baseline diffusion.

</details>


### [31] [On Success and Simplicity: A Second Look at Transferable Vision-Language Attack Pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14974)
*Yuchen Ren,Zhengyu Zhao,Chenhao Lin,Bo Yang,Chao Shen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces a simplified yet effective pipeline for adversarial attacks on Vision-Language Pre-training Models (VLPMs), named SimVLA, which enhances transferability and efficiency over existing methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address vulnerabilities of VLPMs to adversarial attacks while challenging the complexity of current attack strategies.

Method: SimVLA simplifies the attack pipeline by focusing on cross-modal interactions and eliminating excessive complexity in loss functions and processes.

Result: On the Flickr30k dataset, SimVLA outperforms the state-of-the-art (SOTA) baseline in transferability by 8.01%-14.71%, with significantly reduced resource consumption (time and VRAM).

Conclusion: SimVLA shows that leveraging domain knowledge over complex methodologies leads to better performance in adversarial attacks on VLPMs and suggests a straightforward approach for future research.

Abstract: Vision-Language Pre-training Models (VLPMs) are known to be vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Recent transferable attacks on VLPMs have followed a common pipeline with complicated loss functions or multi-stage text/image attacks. However, in this paper, we demonstrate that such a sophisticated attack pipeline can be simpler yet more successful. Specifically, we identify three previously overlooked issues caused by inappropriate cross-modal interactions and excessive operations. To address them, we propose the Simple Vision-Language Attack (SimVLA) pipeline, which observably improves transferability and efficiency. Experiments on four datasets and three downstream tasks validate the superiority of our pipeline. For instance, on Flickr30k text-image retrieval dataset, our SimVLA outperforms the SOTA baseline in R@1 transferability by 8.01\%-14.71\%, while consuming only about 35.73\% of the time and 46.26\% of the max VRAM. Overall, the superiority of our SimVLA highlights the importance of leveraging domain knowledge (e.g., our proposed cross-modal word identification), while blindly pursuing intricate operations (e.g, complex loss functions and redundant multi-stage designs) may even be harmful. We hope our SimVLA can serve as a simple yet effective backbone for future extensions. Code is available at https://github.com/RYC-98/SimVLA.

</details>


### [32] [MagicPrompt: Ultra-Lightweight Prompt Tuning for Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14595)
*Yinhan Zhang,Dinwei Tan,Xianghao Kong,Yue Ma,Yeying Jin,Anyi Rao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MagicPrompt is a lightweight framework for fine-tuning large-scale video diffusion models that improves parameter efficiency and stabilizes training.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the computational costs associated with full fine-tuning of large-scale video diffusion models and overcome limitations of existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods.

Method: MagicPrompt utilizes Attention-Embedded Prompt Tuning for lightweight soft prompts and introduces Dual-Space Reward Feedback Optimization with self-supervised latent objectives to enhance reward training stability.

Result: MagicPrompt achieves competitive performance with less than 1% of trainable parameters and significantly lowers training costs compared to traditional methods.

Conclusion: MagicPrompt offers a highly efficient and stable approach for fine-tuning large-scale VDMs, making it feasible for practical application.

Abstract: Large-scale video diffusion models (VDMs) deliver strong generation performance, but full fine-tuning for downstream tasks incurs prohibitive computational costs. Existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods have two critical flaws on billion-scale models: they still require substantial trainable parameters, and reward-based training suffers from noise-induced optimization instability in condition-guided tasks. We propose MagicPrompt, a lightweight framework that achieves extreme parameter efficiency and stable reward optimization. It first adopts Attention-Embedded Prompt Tuning, which steers generation via lightweight soft prompts with orders of magnitude fewer parameters while preserving pre-trained knowledge. It further introduces Dual-Space Reward Feedback Optimization, which uses self-supervised latent objectives to improve condition-guided reward training. Experiments show MagicPrompt reaches competitive performance with less than 1\% trainable parameters and notably reduces training costs.

</details>


### [33] [Hough-SIFT: Robust Image Registration for Linear Structures via Hough Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14598)
*Masaki Satoh*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Hough-SIFT enhances image registration by applying SIFT in Hough space, maintaining accuracy but improving robustness in linear scenes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the limitations of SIFT in accurately registering images with strong linear structures, which can confuse local feature detection.

Method: Hough-SIFT applies SIFT descriptor matching in Hough space, exploiting distinctive peaks created by linear structures for improved descriptor discriminability.

Result: Experiments show Hough-SIFT is robust in challenging linear scenes where SIFT struggles, yet retains accuracy in typical scenes.

Conclusion: Hough-SIFT offers a reliable solution for image registration in complex scenes, outperforming standard SIFT under specific conditions.

Abstract: Image registration is essential in applications such as electronic image stabilization. Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), a widely used local keypoint detector and descriptor, typically provides accurate registration; however, it often fails in scenes with strong linear structures (e.g., shutters), where local features become ambiguous. We propose Hough-SIFT, a robust registration method that performs SIFT descriptor matching in Hough space. In this domain, linear structures form distinctive peaks that restore descriptor discriminability. Experiments demonstrate that Hough-SIFT is robust in linear scenes where SIFT frequently fails, while maintaining accuracy comparable to SIFT in normal scenes.

</details>


### [34] [Knowing You at First Glance: Inferring Apparent Personality from Faces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14631)
*Shuhuan Chen,Xiangyu Zhu,Weisong Zhao,Haichao Shi,Xiao-Yu Zhang,Zhen Lei*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces GlanceFace, a framework for inferring apparent personality from facial images, emphasizing the use of visual cues and their relation to MBTI types.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Understanding first-impression personality perception based on facial appearance is crucial for enhancing human-robot interaction.

Method: GlanceFace employs vision-language models for semantic priors, a semantic-enhanced facial representation module, and an uncertainty-aware learning strategy for robust performance.

Result: Extensive experiments show strong performance on MBTI-based personality benchmarks, revealing links between facial features and perceived personality traits.

Conclusion: The findings highlight GlanceFace's potential for informing adaptive initial interaction strategies for embodied agents.

Abstract: Inferring apparent personality from facial images is important in social scenarios for embodied agents in human-robot interaction. Unlike inferring intrinsic personality traits via conversation, this task models first-impression personality perception based solely on facial appearance before interaction begins. Existing studies mainly focus on the Big Five personality model and often rely on language or multimodal inputs. As a result, it remains unclear whether facial cues alone can support meaningful associations with perceived personality traits. This question is particularly relevant for MBTI types, which are widely used in practice and more readily interpretable by large language models. To this end, we propose \textbf{GlanceFace}, an end-to-end framework for apparent personality inference leveraging vision-language models to introduce semantic priors and a semantic-enhanced facial representation module to capture subtle personality-related cues, together with an uncertainty-aware learning strategy to handle noisy and subjective annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong performance on MBTI-based apparent personality benchmarks and reveal relationships between facial characteristics and perceived personality traits, highlighting its potential to support adaptive initial interaction strategies for embodied agents. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/MrHuan3/GlanceFace.

</details>


### [35] [Autoregressive Modeling of Film with Applications in Video Montage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14645)
*Marcelo Sandoval-Castañeda,Fabian Caba Heilbron,Shiry Ginosar,Bryan Rusell,Josef Sivic,Alexei A. Efros,Greg Shakhnarovich*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FilmGPT is an autoregressive transformer designed for video montage, transforming unwatchable footage into coherent sequences by learning the grammar of film from data without generating new frames.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the challenge of creating coherent cinematic sequences from unwatchable raw footage by capturing film grammar from data instead of coded rules.

Method: Training a long-context autoregressive transformer on a large movie corpus; using a footage-constrained decoding algorithm for selecting the next shot based on learned statistical patterns.

Result: FilmGPT achieves superior performance on shot sequence ordering benchmarks and improves film editing results significantly compared to previous models, as confirmed by a user study.

Conclusion: FilmGPT is shown to be effective for various video montage applications, including automatic segment trimming and enhanced human-assisted editing.

Abstract: This work introduces FilmGPT, an autoregressive transformer designed to address the challenge of video montage--turning a collection of raw, "unwatchable" footage into coherent cinematic sequences. Inspired by language learning in modern LLMs, we train a long-context autoregressive transformer on a large corpus of movies. The aim is to implicitly capture the "grammar" of film directly from data rather than from hand-coded rules. Unlike other generative models, FilmGPT does not generate any new video frames. Instead, at inference time, we introduce a footage-constrained decoding algorithm to select the best next shot from the input raw footage according to the statistical patterns learned from films. We first evaluate these learned statistics directly by using the FilmGPT autoregressive model for next shot prediction on a standard benchmark of shot sequence ordering, outperforming the previous state of the art. We then evaluate our footage-constrained decoding algorithm on the full film editing task via a user study, and find that our FilmGPT-based editing significantly outperforms previous approaches. Finally, we demonstrate the applicability of FilmGPT to a wide range of applications in video montage, from automatic video segment trimming to human-in-the-loop film editing.

</details>


### [36] [VIABench: A Comprehensive Video Benchmark Collected from Blind Individuals for Visual Impairment Assistance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14660)
*Yunfeng Liu,Yuandong Yang,Jiarui Han,Zhenpeng Huang,Yuqing Tang,Xiangyu Zeng,Gangshan Wu,Limin Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces VIABench, a benchmark for evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in assisting visually impaired individuals with specific tasks using first-person videos. It highlights current limitations of MLLMs in supporting VIIs and aims to drive research towards improved models for real-world applications.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the gap in practical utility of MLLMs for blind assistance, as their capabilities in this domain remain largely unexplored despite advancements in general vision and language tasks.

Method: VIABench defines three core tasks for evaluation: Proactive Reminder, Visual Question Answering, and Vision-Guided Interaction, alongside a rigorous benchmarking pipeline accommodating both online and offline assessments.

Result: Experiments reveal that MLLMs struggle significantly, particularly in the Proactive Reminder task, which requires anticipatory and real-time functionality.

Conclusion: The work aims to inspire further research to tailor MLLMs for real-world use, enhancing navigation and interaction for visually impaired users.

Abstract: Visually impaired individuals (VIIs) encounter significant daily challenges due to limited access to visual information. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive results on general vision and language tasks, their practical utility in real-world blind assistance still remains largely underexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce VIABench, a comprehensive video benchmark specifically designed to evaluate MLLMs in Visually Impaired Assistance scenarios using first-person videos recorded or shared by VIIs themselves. VIABench defines three core tasks, each targeting a distinct requirement in visual assistance. Proactive Reminder: Assesses the model's ability to interpret ongoing video content while proactively anticipating and verbally describing upcoming navigation-critical events; Visual Question Answering (VQA): Evaluates the model's capacity to answer user-posed questions about the environment or objects within the video; Vision-Guided Interaction: Tests context-aware reasoning to accomplish intentional interactions between user and environment. To ensure a robust and fair evaluation, we propose a rigorous benchmarking pipeline that supports both online (real-time) and offline settings. Our experiments demonstrate that current MLLMs still struggle to deliver comprehensive support for VIIs, especially in the Proactive Reminder task, which demands accurate anticipation and real-time responsiveness. We hope VIABench will drive future research toward developing customized MLLMs for real-world assistance, ultimately improving navigation and interaction experiences for visually impaired individuals. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/MCG-NJU/VIABench.

</details>


### [37] [ReBind: Multi-Reference Video Editing via Structured Instructions with Explicit Reference Relationships](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14681)
*Xinyu Liu,Shihao Li,Weihong Lin,Xinlong Chen,Yang Shi,Yujin Han,Yiyang Cai,Yanghao Wang,Ruibin Yuan,Yuanxing Zhang,Pengfei Wan,Wenhan Luo,Yike Guo*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ReBind is a novel framework for improving multi-reference image-conditioned video editing by embedding reference tokens for better coordination and explicit binding between visual attributes and sources.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the inadequacies in existing diffusion-based video generation models in coordinating information from multiple visual sources and improving instruction quality.

Method: ReBind introduces semantic instructions with embedded reference tokens and consists of two components: ReBind-Instruct for establishing explicit bindings via a specialized MLLM, and ReBind-Edit for adapting text-to-video models.

Result: ReBind demonstrates substantial improvements in instruction quality and achieves state-of-the-art performance in reference image conditioned video editing compared to general-purpose MLLMs.

Conclusion: ReBind effectively eliminates ambiguity in visual attribute coordination, offering a systematic approach for enhancing video editing capabilities using multiple references.

Abstract: Recent diffusion-based video generation models have made significant progress in multi-reference image-conditioned video editing. However, existing methods still struggle to coordinate information from multiple visual sources accurately. We identify a critical deficiency in existing approaches. Existing editing instructions lack explicit reference relationships, and most multimodal large language models (MLLMs) cannot generate them reliably. To address this problem, we propose ReBind, a systematic framework that introduces semantic instructions with embedded reference tokens as the intermediate representation for multi-reference image-conditioned video editing. Our key insight is embedding reference tokens at semantic positions to eliminate ambiguity and establish precise bindings between visual attributes and their sources. We develop ReBind-Instruct, a specialized MLLM that learns to establish explicit bindings between visual attributes and their reference sources through a two-stage progressive scheme for precise reference relationships. We further develop ReBind-Edit, which enables lightweight adaptation of text-to-video models to coordinate multiple references by binding visual attributes to their designated sources. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReBind substantially outperforms general-purpose MLLMs in instruction quality and achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source methods on reference image conditioned video editing. Our project webpage: https://rebind-mrv2v.github.io/.

</details>


### [38] [GlobalForge: Towards Robust AI-Generated Image Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14684)
*Manni Cui,Ruiqi Liu,Dianyuan Zou,Ziheng Qin,Jingrui Xu,ZiAn Wang,Jianglan Wei,Han Zhou,Yu Liu,Yan Wang,Shu Wu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GlobalForge improves AIGI detector robustness by shifting focus from local artifacts to global structures, achieving 5.89% better performance on benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AIGI detectors falter under real-world conditions due to overfitting on local artifacts, necessitating a method that emphasizes more resilient features.

Method: Introduced GlobalForge, comprising the Local Information Bottleneck to minimize local shortcut learning, and the Global Structural Reasoning module to enhance feature gathering from distant areas, trained jointly with a contrastive structural loss.

Result: Achieved a 5.89% improvement in average BAcc on 8 in-the-wild benchmark groups compared to previous state-of-the-art, excelling on RealDeg-Bench.

Conclusion: GlobalForge demonstrates enhanced robustness of AIGI detectors against real-world degradations through a novel framework focusing on global structure.

Abstract: AI-generated image (AIGI) detectors achieve strong accuracy on clean benchmarks, but their performance drops sharply after images are propagated through real-world channels. We trace this fragility to what these detectors actually learn: they overfit to local artifacts left by generators in small spatial neighborhoods, which are easily destroyed by common propagation degradations such as JPEG compression and blur. Instead, we shift the discriminative cue from fragile local artifacts to more robust global structure. Building on this, we propose GlobalForge, a framework with two complementary modules. The Local Information Bottleneck (LIB) suppresses local components to block shortcut learning, while the Global Structural Reasoning (GSR) module forces every token to gather evidence from distant regions. Both modules are trained jointly under a contrastive structural loss based on degradation that keeps the resulting features stable under degradation. To support fine-grained robustness evaluation, we further introduce RealDeg-Bench, covering 7 common degradation operators and multi-step compound chains. GlobalForge improves average BAcc on 8 in-the-wild benchmark groups by $\mathbf{5.89\%}$ over the previous state-of-the-art, and is clearly ahead of representative baselines on RealDeg-Bench under both single and compound degradations. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GlobalForge-BE0F/.

</details>


### [39] [Team RAS in 11th ABAW Competition: Multimodal Ambivalence Recognition Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14702)
*Elena Ryumina,Maxim Markitantov,Alexandr Axyonov,Fedor Shchetinin,Timur Abdulkadirov,Dmitry Ryumin,Alexey Karpov*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a novel multimodal approach to recognize ambivalence and hesitancy in videos, leveraging a text-centered model that combines various modalities for improved accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Recognizing ambivalence and hesitancy is complex due to inconsistent expressions across different modes, and existing systems often use resource-intensive ensembles.

Method: The authors propose a Text Residual Fusion model that focuses on text as the primary modality and incorporates gated residual adjustments from other modalities.

Result: The model achieved an average Macro F1-score of 75.14% on Development and Public Test subsets, and 78.24% on the Private Test subset, outperforming a text-only model by 4.03%.

Conclusion: The findings indicate that integrating multimodal information enhances recognition performance efficiently without the need for large model ensembles.

Abstract: Automatic recognition of ambivalence and hesitancy is challenging because these states may be expressed through inconsistent linguistic, acoustic, facial, and contextual patterns, while top-performing systems often rely on computationally expensive ensembles. We present a single text-centered multimodal approach for video-level ambivalence and hesitancy recognition for the 11th Affective & Behavior Analysis in-the-Wild (ABAW) Challenge. The proposed approach combines linguistic, acoustic, facial, and scene features using text-centered multimodal fusion model. Text Residual Fusion treats text as the anchor modality and applies gated residual adjustments based on the other modalities. Experiments on the Behavioural Ambivalence/Hesitancy (BAH) corpus confirm that text is the strongest unimodal modality. The Text Residual Fusion model achieves an average Macro F1-score (MF1) of 75.14% across the Development and Public Test subsets. On the Private Test subset, it reaches an MF1 of 78.24%, outperforming the text model by 4.03%. These results demonstrate that complementary multimodal information can improve recognition performance without requiring a large model ensemble.

</details>


### [40] [Pretraining Multiple Instance Learning Networks with Multi-Teacher Distillation from Pathology Slide Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14703)
*Mingxi Fu,Jiawen Li,Renao Yan,Jiali Hu,Qiehe Sun,Tian Guan,Yonghong He*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a distillation-based pretraining framework for multiple instance learning (MIL) in whole-slide image analysis, addressing challenges of instability and overfitting by using teacher models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing MIL aggregators struggle with unstable optimization and limited transferability due to being trained from scratch with scarce slide-level labels.

Method: The proposed method utilizes two slide-level foundation models as teachers to transfer their knowledge into various MIL architectures, incorporating an angular dispersion normalized distillation loss for balanced supervision.

Result: Pretraining enhances the performance of MIL aggregators across 15 benchmark datasets, particularly in linear probing and few-shot scenarios, while ensuring computational efficiency.

Conclusion: The proposed approach effectively improves upon traditional MIL training, making it more robust and transferrable without compromising the lightweight nature of MIL models.

Abstract: Multiple instance learning (MIL) has become the main paradigm for whole-slide image (WSI) analysis in computational pathology. However, existing MIL aggregators are still typically trained from scratch for each downstream task, relying on limited slide-level labels to learn both aggregation mechanisms and downstream discriminative representations simultaneously. As a result, they often suffer from unstable optimization, overfitting, and limited transferability. Similar to pretrained ResNet and Vision Transformer models in natural image learning, MIL also requires reusable pretrained initialization. However, high-quality slide-level pretraining data remain scarce, and MIL models are usually lightweight and weakly supervised, making large-scale pretraining difficult in practice. To address this challenge, we propose a distillation-based pretraining framework for MIL, which leverages two slide-level foundation models, TITAN and CARE, as teachers to transfer their representational knowledge into a diverse set of MIL architectures. To effectively balance supervision from different teachers, we further introduce an angular dispersion normalized distillation loss. The distilled weights are then used as initialization for downstream adaptation. We conduct systematic evaluations on 15 benchmark datasets under both linear probing and full-parameter fine-tuning, and further validate its advantages in few-shot scenarios. Experimental results show that pretraining generally improves MIL aggregators over from scratch training, especially in linear-probing and few-shot settings, while maintaining the computational efficiency of lightweight MIL models. Code is available at https://github.com/fu0201/MIL_Pretrained.

</details>


### [41] [Variational Inference for Bird's Eye View Segmentation in Autonomous Driving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14710)
*Jingyue Shi,Huaicheng Li,Junhui Zhao,Yanxiang Jiang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents a novel transformer-based network, TVB, for enhancing BEV segmentation in autonomous driving by leveraging variational inference, conditional variational autoencoders, and normalizing flows.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the challenges of fusing data from multiple cameras and operating in complex driving environments for BEV segmentation.

Method: A transformer-based variational flow transformation network (TVB) is proposed, utilizing CVAE and integrating normalizing flows for generating and enhancing BEV maps.

Result: The method produces multiple BEV map candidates and integrates them using a BEV-attention fusion module, resulting in improved performance on nuScenes and OPV2V datasets.

Conclusion: The proposed approach outperforms existing methods in multi-camera view BEV segmentation and lane environment perception, indicating its efficacy in enhancing environmental perception for autonomous driving.

Abstract: The bird's eye view (BEV) has emerged as a pivotal approach for environmental perception in autonomous driving, providing a unified spatial representation for vehicles. Nevertheless, despite BEV's significance in addressing the challenges inherent to autonomous driving, effectively fusing data from multiple camera sensors and operating in complex external driving environments remains a considerable challenge. To mitigate this issue, we recast the BEV segmentation problem within a variational inference framework. In this paper, we propose a novel transformer-based variational flow transformation network for BEV segmentation, denoted as TVB. Our architecture implicitly learns the mapping from multiple camera views to a unified canonical BEV map during training by exploiting posterior BEV supervision. TVB employs a conditional variational auto encoder (CVAE) as its backbone and produces multiple BEV map candidates. To augment the realism of the generated BEV maps, we integrate normalizing flows into the map generation process, enabling the construction of more complex and expressive probability distributions. Furthermore, we design a BEV-attention fusion (BAF) module that harnesses attention mechanisms to adaptively integrate the multiple candidate BEV maps. Experimental results, evaluated on both the nuScenes and OPV2Vdatasets, demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance in multi-camera view BEV segmentation and lane environment perception.

</details>


### [42] [VideoSEMA: a scalable and efficient Mamba-like attention for video understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14711)
*Nhat Thanh Tran,Fanghui Xue andShuai Zhang,Jiancheng Lyu,Yunling Zheng,Yingyong Qi,Jack Xin*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: VideoSEMA is a split space-time attention model for video classification that outperforms existing models in efficiency and accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper aims to improve video understanding through an efficient attention mechanism that combines local and global contexts.

Method: VideoSEMA incorporates a Mamba-like scalable SEMA block for space attention and softmax temporal attention, proving equivalence to full attention under specific conditions.

Result: On benchmark datasets, VideoSEMA surpasses heavier models in efficiency and accuracy, demonstrating enhanced performance as image resolution increases and maintaining leading metrics against similar parameter models.

Conclusion: The results indicate potential for VideoSEMA's application to longer videos with adjustments for temporal attention.

Abstract: We present for video understanding (classification) a split space-time attention model, VideoSEMA, consisting of a scalable and efficient Mamba-like attention (SEMA) block in space and a softmax temporal attention in time. In each frame, SEMA attention applies a local window attention in parallel with a global averaging in a Mamba macro-architecture, which is called Mamba-like. Under certain rank conditions, we prove that the computationally cheaper split space-time attention is equivalent to full space-time attention. On benchmark K400 data sets, VideoSEMA out-performs heavier vision transformer and Mamba models. On benchmark SSv2 data, VideoSEMA leads in top-1 accuracy among models of similar parameter sizes. As image resolution scales up from standard $224^2$ to $1024^2$ on K400 and without fine-tuning, VideoSEMA degrades much more gracefully than VideoMamba in accuracy. It is promising to extend VideoSEMA to longer videos with a dilated/sparse temporal attention.

</details>


### [43] [Causal-Adversarial Probing of Clinical Covariates for Prostate MRI Grading](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14720)
*Yipei Wang,Shiqi Huang,Wen Yan,Weixi Yi,Dean C. Barratt,Mark Emberton,Daniel C. Alexander,Veeru Kasivisvanathan,Yipeng Hu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper introduces a framework to analyze the role of clinical covariates in prostate MRI-based cancer grading using deep learning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To differentiate between useful disease-related signals and non-generalizing shortcut information in deep learning models for prostate MRI-based cancer grading.

Method: A causal-reasoning framework is proposed that uses an adversarial approach to suppress the influence of specific clinical covariates while maintaining MRI-based grade prediction accuracy.

Result: The study analyzes 2,903 prostate MRI exams, revealing that suppressing nuisance variables can improve predictive accuracy, while some clinical variables are essential for effective classification.

Conclusion: Adversarial covariate suppression is a valuable tool for understanding the influence of clinical covariates in prostate MRI grading, highlighting the importance of distinguishing harmful dependence from informative signals.

Abstract: Deep learning models for prostate MRI-based cancer grading may encode clinical covariates that either reflect useful disease-related signal or non-generalising shortcut information, but their role is usually assumed. We propose a causal-reasoning framework for probing covariate dependence in MRI-based International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group prediction. Rather than treating mpMRI as a direct cause of grade, we model MRI appearance and ISUP grade as observations of latent tumour pathology, and test whether candidate clinical variables act as nuisance correlates, disease-related proxies, or irrelevant covariates in the learned representation. We implement this using an adversarial framework that suppresses the decodability of individual clinical covariate at a time while preserving MRI-based grade prediction. The approach is developed and evaluated on 2,903 prostate MRI examinations, with external validation on 576 patients. We report a set of interesting and previously under-explored imaging-to-clinical-variable interactions in the context of deep learning generalisation. For examples, in binary ISUP Grade Group $\geq2$ classification, suppressing age, BMI, and alcohol use improved AUC by 1.23%, 0.84%, and 1.42%, respectively (all p < 0.05), suggesting reduced non-generalising covariate information; In contrast, suppressing PSA and prostate volume degraded AUC by 1.91% and 7.61% (all p < 0.001), indicating that these variables carried task-relevant signal. These findings show that adversarial covariate suppression can provide a practical representation-level analysis for distinguishing potentially harmful dependence from informative signal in prostate MRI grading models.

</details>


### [44] [Multimodality as Supervision: Self-Supervised Specialization to the Test Environment via Multimodality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14721)
*Kunal Pratap Singh,Ali Garjani,Rishubh Singh,Muhammad Uzair Khattak,Efe Tarhan,Jason Toskov,Andrei Atanov,Oğuzhan Fatih Kar,Amir Zamir*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper explores cross-modal learning for device-specific training, presenting Test-Space Training (TST) to leverage multimodal data collection in confined environments, yielding competitive performance without the need for vast internet-scale pre-training datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The study seeks to enhance self-supervision in cross-modal learning by utilizing multimodal sensor data from household robots in controlled environments, informed by insights from developmental psychology on biological representation building.

Method: The authors propose a Test-Space Training (TST) method that involves collecting multimodal data within a specified test environment and conducting self-supervised pre-training on this data.

Result: The findings demonstrate that models trained with TST on multimodal data can achieve competitive performance compared to generalist models pre-trained on large datasets, emphasizing the effectiveness of specialization in limited environments.

Conclusion: The research indicates that cross-modal learning can reduce reliance on extensive external datasets while enhancing model specialization and generalization capabilities across various tasks.

Abstract: Cross-modal learning, i.e., learning to predict one modality from another, is a fundamental mechanism for self-supervision via leveraging multimodality. Many practical applications, e.g., deploying a household robot, involve devices that are equipped with a rich set of sensors that enable multimodal sensing in their test environment. This presents an opportunity to apply cross-modal learning to the multimodal data sensed by these devices to learn representations. Findings in developmental psychology also suggest that biological agents leverage it to build an effective representation of their surroundings.
  To study this, we propose a controlled setup, where we restrict a user device to just a given test environment. It results in a specialization setup where we attempt to develop a performant model for this specific test environment. Under this setup, we develop Test-Space Training (TST), which performs multimodal data collection in the test environment and performs self-supervised pre-training on it. We evaluate these models on various downstream tasks in the same environment.
  Under this setup, we find various interesting insights, such as collecting rich multimodal data only from the test environment and leveraging cross-modal learning, we can achieve competitive results with generalist models (e.g., DINOv2 and CLIP) pre-trained on large-scale internet datasets. This enables an alternative scenario where the need for external Internet-scale datasets for pre-training models is reduced. We also present a set of analyses and ablations that raise intriguing points on substituting data with (multi)modality, and how varying pre-training data enables a tradeoff between a model's abilities to specialise to a test environment, and generalize to held-out spaces.

</details>


### [45] [AE-UAV: An Air-to-Air Event-Based UAV Tracking Benchmark and a Real-Time Frequency-Domain Tracker](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14726)
*Zixin Jiang,Bing He,Chaoran Xiong,Zhenzhen Wang,Xin Zhao,Ling Pei*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents AE-UAV, the first event-based UAV tracking benchmark for air-to-air scenarios, and introduces the Fast-Slow Frequency-domain Tracking (FSFT) method, enabling efficient tracking at high speeds without relying on heavy training or GPU resources.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the challenges in A2A tracking on UAVs, particularly the limitations of traditional cameras under dynamic conditions and the need for practical solutions for resource-constrained systems.

Method: The paper introduces AE-UAV, comprising 178 flight sequences as an event-based dataset, and proposes the FSFT method, which combines frequency-domain template matching with search region prediction, allowing for operation at 420 FPS on CPU hardware.

Result: FSFT maintains 93.97% accuracy compared to GPU-dependent methods while achieving a 5.32-fold speedup and improved temporal resolution generalization.

Conclusion: The proposed AE-UAV benchmark and FSFT method provide an efficient and robust solution for airborne remote sensing, demonstrating the feasibility of effective A2A tracking on UAVs without extensive computational resources.

Abstract: Air-to-air (A2A) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) tracking is fundamental to airborne remote sensing of low-altitude aerial targets. However, the deployment of continuous, real-time tracking systems on UAVs presents significant challenges. In A2A scenarios, traditional frame-based cameras suffer from severe performance degradation under low illumination, overexposure, and high-speed motion owing to their limited dynamic range and fixed temporal sampling. Although event cameras offer a promising alternative with microsecond temporal resolution and a high dynamic range, current research is bottlenecked by two primary issues: 1) the absence of dedicated A2A event-based datasets, and 2) the heavy reliance of existing trackers on GPU acceleration and extensive training data, rendering them impractical for resource-constrained UAVs. To bridge these gaps, we introduce AE-UAV, an air-to-air event-based UAV tracking benchmark. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first airborne-captured event camera dataset for A2A tracking, comprising 178 flight sequences with continuous-time cubic B-spline annotations. Furthermore, we propose the Fast-Slow Frequency-domain Tracking (FSFT) method. This lightweight, training-free framework seamlessly integrates frequency-domain template matching with search region prediction and detection-based drift correction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FSFT operates at an ultra-fast 420 frames per second (FPS) on CPU-only hardware. It retains 93.97% of the accuracy of state-of-the-art GPU-dependent methods while delivering a 5.32-fold effective speedup and exhibiting superior temporal resolution generalization, thereby providing a highly efficient and robust solution for airborne remote sensing of aerial targets. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/MSP-xEN/AE-UAV.

</details>


### [46] [WorkDrive: Roadwork Chain of Causation for Autonomous Driving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14727)
*Tianyi Jiang,Wen Zhang,Sihan Yang,Ming Lu,Wentao Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper introduces WorkDrive, a framework improving autonomous driving in roadwork zones by enhancing visual language models (VLMs) with causal reasoning and trajectory prediction, resulting in reduced trajectory errors.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Autonomous driving VLMs exhibit weaknesses in adapting to altered conditions in roadwork zones, highlighting the need for improved causal reasoning to connect observations to planning decisions.

Method: The WorkDrive framework utilizes a multitask perception pipeline for scene analysis and a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) annotation process to focus on relevant work-zone elements, followed by supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for trajectory prediction.

Result: The proposed CoC approach demonstrated a 9.0% reduction in average displacement error (ADE) on the ROADWork dataset, with an additional 3.0% improvement from consistency-based reinforcement learning, outperforming trajectory-only baselines.

Conclusion: WorkDrive significantly enhances autonomous navigation in roadwork zones leveraging structured reasoning and consistent trajectory predictions, with code and datasets to be made publicly available.

Abstract: Autonomous driving vision-language models (VLMs) struggle in roadwork zones, where familiar visual cues such as lane markings and permanent signs are altered or absent, and temporary devices such as cones and barriers redefine the drivable corridor. VLMs can detect these objects, but without explicit guidance they anchor their reasoning on familiar elements from pre-training and fail to connect work-zone observations to correct planning decisions. We propose WorkDrive, a framework that constructs perception-grounded causal reasoning for work zones and aligns it with trajectory prediction. An automated multitask perception pipeline extracts structured scene facts and injects them into a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) annotation pipeline, redirecting the annotator's attention to domain-specific elements. The resulting reasoning labels are used for supervised fine-tuning, followed by reinforcement learning with a single reward: consistency between lateral meta-actions and the predicted trajectory. On ROADWork, the largest public work-zone dataset, the proposed roadwork CoC reduces trajectory average displacement error (ADE) by 9.0\%, and consistency-based GRPO yields a further 3.0\%, achieving progressive improvement over the trajectory-only baseline. Code and data will be publicly released.

</details>


### [47] [VQ-Touch: A Data-Efficient Tactile Generation Framework Across Sensors and Scenarios](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14728)
*Kailin Lyu,Long Xiao,Jianing Zeng,Di Wu,Lin Shu,Jie Hao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: VQ-Touch is a tactile generation framework that improves tactile data synthesis for robotics by addressing limitations of existing methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper aims to enhance tactile image generation by creating a framework that reduces reliance on expensive sensors and improves generalization and data utilization.

Method: The proposed framework, VQ-Touch, utilizes DM-VQGAN for feature extraction and a discrete diffusion decoder for multimodal tasks and few-shot mixed training.

Result: VQ-Touch demonstrates superior performance over existing methods across various tasks.

Conclusion: The framework effectively supports cross-sensor and multi-scenario applications, advancing tactile perception in robotics and human-machine interaction.

Abstract: Tactile image generation significantly reduces the dependency on expensive and wear-prone sensors by synthesizing high-fidelity tactile data, offering an efficient solution for tactile information acquisition in robotic perception and human-machine interaction systems. However, existing methods depend on large-scale, diverse datasets from specific sensors and lack efficient data utilization and robust generalization capabilities, struggling in vision-limited environments. To address this, we introduce VQ-Touch, a tactile generation framework that supports both cross-sensor and multi-scenario applications. Specifically, to efficiently extract complex deformation and texture features from the data, we propose DM-VQGAN, an effective tactile representation learner. Furthermore, we introduce a discrete diffusion decoder with a unified conditioning interface, supporting multimodal generation tasks such as images and labels, and enhances the model's generalization capability through few-shot mixed training, thus achieving compatibility with current mainstream sensors and their variants. Experiments show that VQ-Touch surpasses state-of-the-art methods in multiple tasks.

</details>


### [48] [GeoDetect: Geometric Adversarial Detection for VLPs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14737)
*Afsaneh Hasanebrahimi,Hanxun Huang,Christopher Leckie,James Bailey,Sarah Erfani*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This study analyzes the vulnerability of vision-language pre-trained models (VLPs) to adversarial attacks and proposes a geometrical approach for detection.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the effectiveness of adversarial detection in multimodal models, specifically VLPs, as existing methods have focused on unimodal settings.

Method: The study investigates the geometry of VLP embedding spaces, highlighting the anisotropic structure and proposing GeoDetect to leverage geometric scores for adversarial detection.

Result: GeoDetect shows a reliable ability to detect adversarial examples across various VLP architectures and threat models, outperforming existing methods.

Conclusion: The approach enhances the safety and reliability of VLPs by effectively detecting adversarial attacks in diverse scenarios.

Abstract: Vision-language pre-trained models (VLPs) are widely used in real-world applications. However, they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Although adversarial detection methods have demonstrated success in single-modality settings (either vision or language), their effectiveness and reliability in multimodal models such as VLPs remain largely unexplored. In this work, we study the geometry of VLP embedding spaces and observe structured anisotropy that differs from unimodal vision models. Our theoretical analysis shows that under this anisotropic structure, adversarial attacks increase the expected geometric separation between clean and adversarial examples (AEs). Specifically, we demonstrate that AEs consistently exhibit greater expected distances to randomly sampled points than their clean counterparts, indicating that AEs tend to push representations out of manifold regions. Building on these insights, we propose GeoDetect, which leverages these off-manifold deviations via geometric scores to identify AEs. Through comprehensive evaluations, we show that our approach reliably detects AEs across diverse VLP architectures and threat settings, covering unimodal and multimodal attacks as well as adaptive attacks, thereby providing a robust and practical approach to improving the safety and reliability of these models.

</details>


### [49] [FoMoVLA: Bridging Visual Foresight and Motion Guidance for Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14739)
*Wei Li,Peijin Jia,Yuan Ma,Xuefeng Jiang,Titong Jiang,Sheng Sun,Yujian Li,Xin Wen,Han Hong,Zhikang Liu,Bailin Li,Kun Zhan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FoMoVLA enhances VLA models by integrating future feature prediction and sparse point tracking for improved visuomotor policy learning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current VLA models are reactive, lacking forward prediction of dynamics to guide motion in visuomotor tasks.

Method: FoMoVLA augments VLA representations with spatio-temporal supervision, learning future feature foresight and sparse 2D point tracking through a cross-attention module.

Result: Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks such as LIBERO and RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop, with notable zero-shot generalization.

Conclusion: FoMoVLA effectively combines prediction and tracking for better continuous action policy in VLA models.

Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have achieved impressive results in visuomotor policy learning, yet remain fundamentally reactive, mapping current observations and language to actions without explicit forward prediction of world dynamics. Existing visual foresight methods predict future visual states but lack explicit motion guidance: they show where to go but not how to get there. We argue that future feature prediction and sparse point tracking are naturally complementary: the former provides the goal state, while the latter captures the continuous motion path toward it. We propose FoMoVLA, a framework that augments VLA representations with explicit spatio-temporal supervision by jointly learning future feature foresight and sparse 2D point tracking, enhancing the continuous action policy. FoMoVLA introduces compact foresight tokens to decode future feature states, decodes sparse temporal 2D point trajectories to model compact geometric motion, and couples both through a lightweight future-conditioned cross-attention module that enables consistent reasoning between anticipated states and point dynamics. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop, and LIBERO-Plus demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and strong zero-shot generalization. Project page is available at https://liauto-research.github.io/FoMoVLA.

</details>


### [50] [On the Disagreement in Perturbation-based xAI -- Benchmarking Perturbation Choices for Flood Detection from SAR Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14743)
*Anastasia Schlegel,Ronny Hänsch*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper investigates the impact of perturbation method parameters on relevance estimation in explainable AI (xAI) for deep learning models, particularly in flood detection from radar imagery.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the sensitivity of perturbation-based xAI methods to different parameter choices, which may lead to inconsistent or misleading relevance maps.

Method: The study examines the effects of two parameters: patch geometry (size and shape of perturbed regions) and perturbation type (replacement scheme) through a thorough investigation in the context of flood detection from Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery.

Result: Findings reveal that varying perturbation settings significantly affects the relevance maps, leading to ambiguous and contradictory explanations.

Conclusion: The results underline the necessity of scrutinizing perturbation parameters in xAI methodologies to ensure accurate interpretations of explanations and model predictions.

Abstract: Perturbation-based xAI methods are widely used to analyze the behavior and predictions of deep learning models. By altering input regions and measuring the resulting changes in class probabilities with respect to the original image, they assign relevance scores and generate heatmaps that reflect each region's contribution to the prediction. Despite their apparent simplicity, however, perturbation-based methods are sensitive to parameter choices. In this work, we focus on two key parameters of the perturbation pipeline, namely the patch geometry, including the size and shape of the perturbed regions, and the perturbation type, defined by the replacement scheme. Grounded in the use case of flood detection from Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of how relevance estimation changes under different perturbation settings. Beyond visual inspection of the resulting relevance maps, we evaluate their consistency across perturbation strategies and their faithfulness to the model's reasoning. We demonstrate how different perturbation choices can steer the resulting relevance maps, yielding ambiguous and even contradictory explanations. Our findings emphasize the importance of methodological settings in perturbation-based xAI. They underscore the need to carefully inspect and evaluate perturbation choices and to treat them as an integral part when interpreting explanations, ensuring a robust understanding of both the explanations and model predictions.

</details>


### [51] [Clean-Reference Streaming Detection of Lens Occlusion and Photometric Transitions for Camera Tamper Monitoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14760)
*Bo Ma,WeiQi Yan,Jinsong Wu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper proposes a narrow streaming integrity monitor for surveillance cameras that detects sensor faults due to lens occlusion and abrupt scene transitions, achieving low false alarms and high recall rates.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the silent degradation of surveillance cameras that affects data integrity and to ensure reliable monitoring with low false alarm rates.

Method: The study uses a detector that analyzes luminance and local-gradient statistics against a clean-only reference, employing techniques for light rejection and brightness suppression, issuing minimal notifications per tamper instance.

Result: The integrity monitor achieved an F1 score of 0.800 and a balanced accuracy of 0.822 on controlled sequences, with notable recall rates and low false positives during stress tests.

Conclusion: The proposed method effectively functions as an auditable subsystem for sensor health, rather than a general-purpose tamper classifier, with a focus on sustaining low false alarms.

Abstract: A surveillance camera is an image sensor whose silent physical degradation invalidates every downstream consumer of its data. In-situ integrity alarms for such vision sensors require low false-alarm rates, bounded computation, and diagnosable behavior under nuisance illumination changes. This paper studies a deliberately narrow streaming integrity monitor for two low-cost sensor-fault signatures: texture-collapsing lens occlusion and abrupt photometric scene transition. The detector compares sampled luminance and local-gradient statistics with a clean-only sliding reference, applies coarse-grid structured-light rejection and mode/rapid-brightness suppression, and emits at most one notification per tamper episode. We formalize the decision predicates and derive a consistency rule for when rapid-brightness suppression makes the scene-transition path unreachable. On 320 in-scope controlled sequences, the default state machine attains 0.800 F1 and 0.822 balanced accuracy (significantly better paired correctness than the strongest baseline, though the F1 margin is not statistically resolved); on a magnitude-swept public audit it attains the highest partial AUC under a 5\% false-alarm budget, and a separate extended-stress FPR-constrained sweep reaches 0.925 recall at 0.025 false-positive rate. Public Xiph, Bremen IoT, and UHCTD diagnostics show the fixed predicates preserve low false alarms while recall concentrates inside the declared envelope (UHCTD in-scope covered recall 0.667 versus 0.016 out of scope), and a 9.09-camera-hour verified-negative public audit records zero false alarms. The method is best interpreted as an auditable sensor-health subsystem rather than a universal camera-tamper classifier.

</details>


### [52] [Rare Concept Generation via Counterfactual Inference in Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14765)
*Zhengyuan Jiang,Haipeng Liu,Meng Wang,Yang Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CI-Diff addresses the challenge of generating images with rare concepts by mitigating common knowledge bias in diffusion models, employing counterfactual inference to improve attribute rendering and concept composition.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Previous image generation models struggle with accurately rendering unusual attributes in rare concepts due to common knowledge bias, necessitating a better method.

Method: The CI-Diff approach employs counterfactual inference to filter out common knowledge bias and reformulates classifier-free guidance to emphasize atypical attributes for more accurate image generation.

Result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that CI-Diff outperforms existing state-of-the-art diffusion models on the RareBench benchmark.

Conclusion: CI-Diff introduces a novel causal inference methodology to rare concept generation, showcasing its effectiveness and superiority in generating images with rare attributes.

Abstract: Rare concept generation focuses on synthesizing customized images conditioned on text prompts that describe objects with unusual attributes. Previous works failed to align the generated images with rare concepts, resulting in incorrect attribute rendering or inconsistent composition of concepts. Such failures, as we observed, stem from the inherent common knowledge bias in the training stage of diffusion models, where objects are strongly associated with their common attributes, making it difficult to break these associations when generating rare concepts. To address such challenges, in this paper, we propose a novel Counterfactual Inference-based Diffusion approach, dubbed CI-Diff. CI-Diff blocks the interference of the model's inherent common knowledge bias and utilizes the Natural Direct Effect to capture the independent influence of the text prompt of rare concepts on image generation so that decoupling the unusual attributes from the rare concepts. To this end, we reformulate the classifier-free guidance mechanism to highlight the atypical attributes. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to introduce causal inference into the rare concept generation task. Extensive experiments on the RareBench benchmark validate the superiority of CI-Diff over state-of-the-art diffusion models. Our code can be accessed from https://github.com/200204jzy/CI-Diff.

</details>


### [53] [TAMF-VTON: Texture-Aware Mask-Free Virtual Try-On via High-Fidelity Image Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14807)
*Jie Wang,Qian He,Gaofeng He,Xiaogang Jin,Huamin Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TAMF-VTON is a novel texture-aware, mask-free framework for virtual try-on that overcomes limitations of existing methods, enabling high-fidelity image synthesis with support for diverse garment compositions while ensuring efficient inference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address challenges in existing VTON methods, such as reliance on segmentation masks and poor texture preservation, while enabling scalable deployment in e-commerce.

Method: A unified generative pipeline featuring a Mixture-of-Experts adaptation, frequency-domain supervision for texture consistency, and adaptive inpainting for training data curation.

Result: TAMF-VTON outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and perceptual quality, achieving efficient inference in under 15 seconds per image on consumer hardware.

Conclusion: The framework supports mask-free operations, multi-garment compositions, and faithful texture preservation, making it a viable solution for real-world digital fashion applications.

Abstract: Recent diffusion-based virtual try-on (VTON) methods remain limited by their reliance on segmentation masks, insufficient preservation of fine-grained textures, and limited support for arbitrary multi-garment compositions. Consequently, existing approaches still face significant challenges in real-world e-commerce deployment. We present TAMF-VTON, a texture-aware, mask-free framework that enables high-fidelity image synthesis under practical unconstrained conditions. Our method requires no human parsing or inpainting masks at inference time and supports diverse garment styles, categories, and quantities, enabling the simultaneous transfer of multiple items while preserving body structure and intricate texture details. This is achieved through a unified generative pipeline with three key components: (1) a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) adaptation scheme that enables efficient fine-tuning without compromising the base model's general editing capabilities; (2) a frequency-domain supervision mechanism that explicitly optimizes high-frequency spectral consistency to preserve high-fidelity textures; and (3) a robust data curation pipeline employing an adaptive inpainting strategy to simulate the inverse VTON process for high-quality training pair generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and perceptual quality. Optimized for efficiency, the model achieves inference in under 15 seconds per image on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with INT4 quantization. By combining mask-free operation, flexible multi-garment composition, faithful texture preservation, and efficient inference on consumer hardware, TAMF-VTON demonstrates a commercially viable solution for scalable deployment in real-world digital fashion scenarios. The project is available at https://www.style3d.ai/ai-photoshoot/virtual-clothing-try-on.

</details>


### [54] [An LLM-Based Automatic Sportscast Solution for Robot Soccer Matches](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14809)
*Francesco Petri,Michele Brienza,Daniele Nardi,Domenico Daniele Bloisi,Aldo Gangemi,Vincenzo Suriani*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a real-time autonomous sports commentator for RoboCup soccer matches that generates precise statistics and fluent narration from kinematic tracking data.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To measure research progress towards solving real-world problems in RoboCup, particularly aiming for the 2050 FIFA World Cup, through effective commentary and statistics analysis.

Method: The paper proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture that processes match video streams to extract statistics and generate commentary in real-time and post-game analysis.

Result: The system provides accurate, hallucination-free narration and adapts to diverse humanoid robots in dynamic soccer matches.

Conclusion: This autonomous commentator enhances the understanding of match dynamics and showcases the integration of AI in sports commentary.

Abstract: RoboCup has always been a scenario to develop systems that solve real-world problems. Driven by the main goal of playing against the 2050 FIFA World Cup champions, the RoboCup Soccer leagues need to constantly measure how the research community is progressing. Computing visual statistics from match videos is a crucial way to track this evolution. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a fully autonomous, real-time sports commentator for RoboCup matches. By bridging the gap between raw kinematic tracking and natural language generation, our neuro-symbolic architecture extracts precise statistics from video streams and turns them into fluent, hallucination-free narration. The proposed system is capable of generating statistics and commentary both during live match streaming and in post-game analysis, easily adapting to the new dynamism of the league where different humanoid robots of different sizes share the field. Supplemental materials are available at https://lab-rococo-sapienza.github.io/MARIO/

</details>


### [55] [Blurring Modal Boundaries: A Unified Survey from Single- to Multi-Modal Person Re-ldentification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14821)
*Xiao Wang,Bing Wang,Bin Yang,Cuiqun Chen,Xin Xu,Mang Ye*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper surveys the evolution of person re-identification (ReID) methods from traditional RGB approaches to cross-modal and multi-modal strategies, highlighting key tasks and proposing a Transformer-based baseline framework for visible-infrared ReID.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation behind this survey is to address limitations in traditional ReID methods by exploring cross-modal and multi-modal approaches that can enhance identity matching in challenging environments.

Method: The paper systematically reviews various cross-modal ReID tasks, focusing on visible-infrared, text-image, sketch-based, and Non-Line-of-Sight ReID, while also proposing a Transformer-based baseline framework.

Result: The survey highlights advances in ReID techniques and proposes a framework that effectively captures modality-invariant features, allowing for improved matching across different modalities.

Conclusion: The authors conclude by discussing the current landscape of ReID research and suggesting future directions that could further enhance person re-identification performance.

Abstract: Person re-identification (ReID) serves as a critical component in intelligent surveillance systems, aiming to match identities across disjoint camera networks. While traditional methods primarily rely on single-modal RGB imagery, they are often constrained by environmental challenges such as low illumination and occlusion. To overcome these limitations, the field is rapidly evolving toward cross-modal and multi-modal paradigms. This survey presents a comprehensive overview of this transition, systematically reviewing key cross-modal tasks including visible-infrared (VI-ReID), text-image (TI-ReID), sketch-based (Sketch-ReID), and the emerging Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) ReID, which extends perception beyond direct visibility. Furthermore, we examine tri-spectral and multi-modal fusion ReID, discussing how complementary information from diverse sensors enhances robustness. Beyond summarizing datasets, challenges, and methodologies, we propose a Transformer-based baseline framework for visible-infrared ReID, designed to effectively capture modality-invariant features. Finally, based on the current landscape, we outline several promising directions for future research.

</details>


### [56] [SUFLECA: Scaling Up Feature Learning for CAD-to-image Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15058)
*Saad Ejaz,Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas,Javier Civera,Holger Voos,Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SUFLECA proposes a weakly-supervised framework for CAD-to-image alignment that improves alignment accuracy and computational efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance CAD-to-image alignment accuracy and address the limitations of existing appearance-driven zero-shot methods, particularly under occlusion and domain shifts.

Method: A weakly-supervised approach utilizing Normalized Object Coordinates (NOCs) for geometry-grounded feature learning, combined with a consistent matching algorithm for establishing reliable correspondences between CAD models and images.

Result: SUFLECA achieves category/instance accuracy of 33.4%/42.3% on ScanNet25k, outperforming previous zero-shot and even fully supervised methods with a reduced computational footprint.

Conclusion: The contributions of SUFLECA lead to efficient and accurate CAD-to-image alignment, making it a significant advancement in the field.

Abstract: CAD-to-image alignment aims to estimate an object's 9D pose (rotation, translation, and anisotropic scale) from a single RGB image, enabling applications in robotics and augmented reality. Recent zero-shot methods use visual foundation models to match image regions to CAD models, yet typically their correspondences are appearance-driven and degrade under occlusion or sim-to-real domain shift. To address these limitations, we introduce SUFLECA (Scaling Up Feature LEarning for CAD Alignment), a weakly-supervised framework for zero-shot CAD alignment with two key contributions. First, SUFLECA scales up geometry-grounded feature learning from pretrained visual representations through Normalized Object Coordinates (NOCs) supervision on 674K images spanning 12 real and synthetic datasets, learning compact geometry-aware features that generalize across domains. Second, we propose a geometrically consistent matching algorithm that establishes reliable one-to-one CAD-to-image correspondences. Together, these contributions enable accurate, sub-second alignment per object instance without iterative pose refinement. On ScanNet25k, SUFLECA achieves 33.4%/42.3% category/instance accuracy, outperforming, with a smaller computational footprint, the strongest zero-shot baseline by 10.3/12.2 percentage points and, for the first time on this benchmark, even surpassing fully supervised methods. Code is available at: https://github.com/snt-arg/SUFLECA

</details>


### [57] [Physics-Informed Diffusion for Biomechanically Plausible 3D Sign Language Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14836)
*Emanuele Colonna,Moises Diaz,Gennaro Vessio,Miguel Angel Ferrer,Giovanna Castellano*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PIDiffSign is a physics-informed diffusion model that improves sign language generation by enforcing anatomical constraints, enhancing both motion realism and semantic fidelity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for accurate sign language production that conveys meaning while adhering to biomechanical constraints.

Method: PIDiffSign employs a Transformer encoder-decoder structure, applies a differentiable geometry module for anatomical consistency, and combines various constraints with a contrastive gloss-pose alignment loss during training.

Result: Experiments indicate significant improvements in pose accuracy, joint-angle correctness, distributional realism, and back-translation quality when compared to a baseline model.

Conclusion: The physics-informed approach in PIDiffSign effectively enhances the generated sign language motions, achieving better realism and fidelity.

Abstract: Sign language production, which generates continuous 3D skeletal motion from spoken language input, must simultaneously satisfy two constraints: semantic fidelity, so that a deaf viewer can recognize the intended sequence of glosses, and biomechanical plausibility, so that the generated skeleton respects anatomical constraints. Existing approaches optimize semantic reconstruction through coordinate-based objectives that treat the skeleton as an unstructured vector, thus allowing for bone length drift, joint angle violations, and temporarily locked fingers. We introduce PIDiffSign, a physics-informed diffusion model for gloss-to-pose translation that incorporates anatomical constraints into both the architecture and training objective. The model uses a Transformer encoder-decoder, where the decoder is conditioned on the diffusion time step through adaptive zero-initialized layer normalization and cross-attends to gloss representations. A differentiable geometry module enforces bone length consistency and biologically valid joint angles throughout generation. Training combines anthropomorphic, kinematic, angular, and finger-joint constraints with a contrastive gloss-pose alignment loss and classifier-free guidance for semantically conditioned sampling. Experiments on the PHOENIX14T and CSL-Daily benchmarks show consistent improvements over a strong diffusion baseline in pose accuracy, joint-angle correctness, distributional realism, and back-translation quality. These results demonstrate that physics-informed diffusion improves both motion realism and semantic fidelity for sign language generation.

</details>


### [58] [Rotational Motion-Induced Error Compensation for Phase-Shifting Profilometry-Based Eye Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14876)
*Seong-Jin An,Sanghoon Jeon,Yatong An,Jae-Sang Hyun*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a method for improving the accuracy of 3D eye reconstruction using Phase-Shifting Profilometry (PSP) by compensating for motion-induced errors during eye rotation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for reliable eye tracking in VR/AR applications motivates the development of more stable and accurate 3D eye reconstruction methods.

Method: The authors propose a motion compensation framework for PSP that estimates eye rotation from image-based cues and adjusts for errors due to inter-frame rotation, alongside a region-wise optimization strategy to minimize artifacts.

Result: Experiments show that the method effectively reduces motion-induced deformation and enhances reconstruction accuracy, applicable beyond spherical eye geometry.

Conclusion: The study provides a solid foundation for advancing high-precision eye tracking in immersive environments through improved dynamic 3D eye reconstruction.

Abstract: With the proliferation of immersive Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) for Virtual and Augmented Reality (VR/AR), reliable and high-precision eye tracking has become increasingly important. Conventional 2D image-based methods offer low system complexity but remain limited in stability, accuracy, and robustness. Three-dimensional ocular surface reconstruction can provide richer geomet-ric information, and structured light profilometry is particularly attractive because it enables dense and accurate surface measurement. However, Phase-Shifting Profilometry (PSP), which estimates phase from sequentially acquired fringe images, is highly susceptible to motion-induced errors when the eye rotates between frames. This study proposes a rotational motion compensation framework for PSP-based dynamic 3D eye reconstruction. Relative eye rotation is estimated from image-based motion cues using a user-specific 3D eye model in a spherical-coordinate domain. The estimated motion is then used to compensate for camera-pixel mismatch and phase-shift errors caused by inter-frame rotation. A region-wise optimization strategy is further introduced to reduce residual artifacts by inde-pendently refining the compensation strength in different ocular regions. Experiments with a rotating fake eye under non-uniform motion demonstrate that the proposed method substantially suppresses motion-induced deformation and improves reconstruction accuracy. An additional experiment with a non-spherical rigid object indicates that the compensation principle is not restricted to spherical eye geometry. These results establish a practical basis for stable PSP-based dynamic 3D eye reconstruction toward future high-precision eye tracking in immersive environments.

</details>


### [59] [Selectivity Drives Efficiency: Dataset Pruning for Visual Place Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14897)
*Tong Jin,Yunpeng Liu,Shuyu Hu,Chun Yuan,Song Wang,Feng Lu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a place-wise dataset pruning framework for visual place recognition, which improves data efficiency and model performance by focusing on place-level rather than image-level pruning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The reliance on large-scale datasets in visual place recognition leads to high storage and training costs, necessitating more efficient data utilization.

Method: The proposed method prunes datasets based on place-wise metrics: intra-place diversity (IPD) and inter-place similarity (IPS), ranking places for selection to form a compact coreset.

Result: The new framework shows consistent improvements over existing dataset pruning methods, achieving higher accuracy with reduced dataset size and training costs.

Conclusion: The place-wise pruning method maintains competitive performance in visual place recognition while significantly reducing the dataset size and training resources needed.

Abstract: Recent visual place recognition (VPR) studies have increasingly relied on large-scale datasets to train more robust and discriminative models. Although this trend significantly improves recognition performance, it also introduces substantial storage and training costs, especially when new architectures or training strategies need to be repeatedly developed and evaluated. Dataset pruning (DP) provides a promising way to improve data efficiency by retaining only informative training data. However, conventional DP methods mainly follow the sample-wise classification paradigm, which overlooks the relation-dependent training nature of VPR, where supervision is typically formed by image pairs rather than independent images. To address this issue, we propose a place-wise dataset pruning framework tailored for VPR. Instead of pruning individual images, our method treats each place as the basic pruning unit and introduces two complementary novel metrics, i.e., intra-place diversity (IPD) and inter-place similarity (IPS), to evaluate the training value of each place. By jointly considering these two metrics, our method ranks all places and constructs a compact yet informative coreset, thereby allowing the pruned dataset to still support the training of robust and discriminative VPR models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art DP baselines under different pruning ratios while reducing selection and training costs. Moreover, by pruning a merged dataset roughly 3.5$\times$ the size of GSV-Cities to a comparable scale, our coreset maintains highly competitive performance, achieving 94.5\% R@1 on MSLS-val and 97.0\% R@1 on Nordland with only NetVLAD. Codes will be made publicly available.

</details>


### [60] [FlashDecoder: Real-Time Latent-to-Pixel Streaming Decoder with Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14898)
*Minguk Kang,Suha Kwak*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FlashDecoder is a fast, memory-efficient, pure-Transformer video decoder that improves real-time video generation by processing frames sequentially and attending to a fixed number of past frames, achieving performance similar to convolutional decoders with significantly reduced latency and memory usage.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for efficient real-time video generation that balances fast decoding and denoising capabilities, particularly for high-resolution and long videos, which is hindered by the limitations of current 3D convolutional decoders.

Method: FlashDecoder employs a pure-Transformer architecture that decodes video frames sequentially, using a rolling key-value (KV) cache to attend to a fixed-size window of past frames, thus ensuring rapid processing and low memory usage.
